text:
maria_support: FYI, customer reported 502s then suddenly responses changed format after what looks like a region failover. they say APAC users got very short, garbled replies. attaching paste of request/response.

maria_support: Customer note: "At 2025-11-17T03:44:11Z we saw timeouts then a bunch of responses that look like tokenized fragments, e.g. 'Ġ��� the' and missing sections. This started right after a flurry of 503s."

maria_support: Minimal repro payload from customer:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Region-Hint: ap-southeast-1
{
  "model": "redwood-base-1.2",
  "input": "Summarize the attached invoice...",
  "stream": false
}
```

maria_support: Attach logs they forwarded (sanitized):
```
req_id=ri-9f7a t=1709997851 route=ap-southeast-1 served_by=eu-west-2
model_variants=[redwood-lite-1.3_quant]
status=200 body_snippet="Ġ��� the"
```

sanjay_eng-runtime: pinging. can you paste one full request_id from the customer? need to correlate with router traces.

maria_support: req_id ri-9f7a in logs above, customer provided that one. they also sent a sample response with token bytes garbled.

ingrid_oncall: deploy-bot shows a node OOM in ap-southeast at 03:43:58Z and automated failover engaged a standby pool in eu-west-2 at 03:44:02Z. I'm seeing routing policy had 'regional-standby' set to true for that pool.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] node/instance ap-southeast-1/gpu-12 crashed (OOM) at 2025-11-17T03:43:58Z; standby-range=eu-west-2 selected by router v2.4.1

sanjay_eng-runtime: OK, that explains cross-region failover. Question: why was the eu standby serving a different variant? router should only select compatible tokenizer-compatible variants. checking router logs now.

ops-bot: [ops-bot] routing decision for req=ri-9f7a: region_hint=ap-southeast-1 -> candidate_pool=eu-west-2-standby -> selected_variant=redwood-lite-1.3_quant (variant_tokenizer=vocab-v2)

kevin_prod: redwood-lite variants are in the compatible family but the quantized build shipped with a trimmed vocab (vocab-v2) last week to save RAM. that explains the tokenizer mismatch. we didn't mark it as 'incompatible' because we assumed full vocab parity.

sanjay_eng-runtime: that mismatch can cause weird byte sequences when decoding. immediate mitigation: block automatic fallback to pools that advertise trimmed tokenizers. can we add a runtime guard? also need to tell support what to tell the customer.

ingrid_oncall: I can flip a flag to disable cross-region standby fallback for ap-southeast-1 until we push a fix. doing it now (will affect resilience briefly).

ingrid_oncall: done — regional-standby disabled for ap-southeast-1 at 03:45:20Z. please confirm.

sanjay_eng-runtime: confirmed. also created a short-term router patch to prefer same-tokenizer variants (PR #3982). will land in canary in 10m.

maria_support: Customer needs a clear workaround. Suggested message: "We've temporarily disabled cross-region standby for APAC to restore your original model routing. If you need immediate continuity, please set model=redwood-base-1.2 (this pins to the base family) or add header X-Prefer-Region: ap-southeast-1. We're pushing a platform fix."

kevin_prod: let's also add a server-side policy that refuses to route to a variant whose tokenizer_id != requested_model.tokenizer_id. that will prevent this class of silent swaps.

sanjay_eng-runtime: agreed. I'm opening INC-22511 to track this and the followups: include rollback of trimmed-vocab quant builds OR mark them as incompatible in catalog.

sanjay_eng-runtime: reproduction notes for eng team:
1) simulate node OOM in ap-southeast-1
2) allow router to select eu-west-2-standby
3) serve quantized-lite variant with trimmed vocab
4) observe decoding artifacts as shown above

maria_support: Customer reply: "Thanks, setting X-Prefer-Region fixed it for now, responses look normal. Please keep us updated." :relieved:

ingrid_oncall: filing a postmortem entry and scheduling a working session with models for tokenizer parity. tagging kevin and runtime.

kevin_prod: will add a catalog flag 'tokenizer_compatible' and backfill current variants. also auditing recent quant builds.

sanjay_eng-runtime: next steps: (a) router patch -> canary -> prod (b) catalog compatibility flag (c) incident INC-22511 updates. ETA for router patch rollout 2h, catalog change 1d.

maria_support: Thanks all. I'll close the support loop with the customer and reference INC-22511 and the quick workaround. closing note: customer asked if billing was affected — they were charged normally for the requests; confirmed from billing logs. no adjustments needed but we're monitoring.

kevin_prod: add to postmortem: risk of silent capability regression when fallback pools have trimmed artifacts. action item: ensure variant metadata includes tokenizer_id and capability_flags.

sanjay_eng-runtime: assigning owners: router=ingrid_oncall, catalog=kevin_prod, runtime=sanjay_eng-runtime. will update INC-22511 with progress.

maria_support: customer says "app regained stability, thanks" — marking resolved from our side. :white_check_mark:
